prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-19. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 2.29 |
| Retained earnings       | 3,431M |
| Current liabilities     | 5,712M |
| Current assets          | 13,066M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 33,867M |
| Total liabilities       | 23,079M |
| Total assets            | 57,121M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,688M |
| Revenue                 | 6,571M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-19, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided balance sheet shows low leverage (equity/assets ≈ 59%, total liabilities/assets ≈ 40%) and solid liquidity (current ratio of 2.29). Operating margins are exceptionally high (EBIT/revenue ≈ 56%), supporting strong debt-service capacity despite the modest scale of revenue relative to the asset base. These metrics are consistent with an upper-medium-grade credit profile, though the low retained-earnings balance relative to equity leaves some uncertainty about earnings persistence.
DECISION: A
